_note: Recipes for tools/spritegen.py. Each entry names a SOURCE already in assets/ and a chain of ops,
and writes a new set that keeps the source's filenames -- which is what makes the result loadable
by the probing loaders already in 08c_embersprites.js.
WHY THE ELEMENTS ARE BUILT OUT OF `ramp` AND NOT `hue`, which is the one thing to understand
before editing this file. `hue: {to: N}` rotates a sprite's existing colour toward a target, so
what it produces depends on the colour the source already had -- and it is measured against the
sprite's DOMINANT hue, which on a two-colour sprite is a lie. arch_golem reports 324 degrees, a
magenta it does not contain anywhere: it is a violet core and warm stone averaging out. A single
`hue` delta across that moved the red trim to yellow while the core went blue.
`ramp` is driven by LUMINANCE instead, which every sprite has and which does not vary by
archetype. That is what lets one element definition land identically on a golem, a husk and a
plant -- verified on all three -- so the shared table below is genuinely shared and not twelve
copies drifting apart. Use `hue` for BESPOKE per-sprite work, with `only` to name the band, and
run `--probe <path>` first to find out what the bands are.
`ramp.mix` is the dial. Measured on this art: 0.45 barely reads, 0.75 flattens the accent trim
that carries the creature's identity, 0.58 keeps the trim and still reads as a different element
across the room. Start at 0.58 and only move it with a contact sheet open.
NAMING IS YOURS AT THREE LEVELS, and the default of 'keep the source's names' is only a default.
`to`      names the set and where it lands; {v} is the variant name. See still_hound.
`as`      renames variants of ONE recipe without touching the shared table they came from --
which is the point, since eleven other archetypes are reading that same table.
`rename`  names the individual FRAMES, either as a pattern over the tokens
{stem} source name without .png    {base} that with any trailing _<n> removed
{n}    trailing frame number       {v} variant   {set} recipe   {ext} '.png'
e.g. "rename": "{base}_{v}_{n}{ext}"   ->  idle_3.png becomes idle_frost_3.png
or as an explicit MAP for full per-file control, which only renames what it lists:
"rename": {"idle_0.png": "sleep_0.png", "attack_0.png": "lunge_0.png"}
A variant may also be written long-hand as an object with its own `name`, `to`, `ops` and
`rename`, which lets a single member of a family land somewhere else entirely.
Two frames colliding on one output name is refused outright rather than letting the last write
win, and `--show-names` prints every source -> output name without writing anything. Renaming off
the loaders' `idle_/walk_/attack_/ride_` pattern only warns -- you may well mean it.
AFTER BUILDING: look at the contact sheet (--sheet), then bump ART_CACHE in sw.js.

still_crab.note: Archetype stills, four elements each. One file per variant -- the whole set of twelve archetypes is 48 files and about 200 KB, which is why the stills are all here and the animations are not.

still_hound.note: THE WORKED EXAMPLE FOR NAMING. The elements are shared across all twelve archetypes, but nothing says this recipe has to accept their names: `as` renames them here and only here, and `to` puts them wherever you like -- so the hound families are cinderhound/rimehound/nighthound/plaguehound rather than hound_ember and friends, while the other eleven archetypes keep using the same element definitions untouched. Recipe names follow the output names, so this builds as still_hound_rimehound.

anim_golem.note: The animated families: 18 frames (idle x9 + attack x9) per variant, so ONE archetype is 72 files. Four archetypes are animated here rather than twelve, deliberately -- all twelve would be 864 files and ~7 MB of art cache, and that is a decision to take on purpose rather than by running a tool once. Extending it is one entry per archetype, copied from this one.

elite_golem.note: The ELITE treatment, and the reason `pad` exists: the halo needs room the source frame does not have, so pad FIRST and pad every frame by the same amount or the animation jitters. Colour only -- an elite is the same creature wearing the fact that it is dangerous, and the silhouette has to stay the thing the player already learned to recognise.

spectral_wisp.note: Phantom/spectral. `alpha` is nearly the whole treatment -- a spectre is a transparency problem, not a colour one, and every attempt to say it with colour alone reads as 'blue wisp'.

golem_corebands.note: THE WORKED EXAMPLE FOR `only`. arch_golem probes as three bands: warm stone at 0-60, a violet core at 270-300, red trim at 330-360. This takes the core to cold blue and leaves the stone and the trim exactly where they are -- which is the one thing `ramp` cannot do, because ramp touches every pixel. Bespoke, per-sprite, and it will NOT transfer to another archetype: run `--probe` on that one and read its own bands.
